chapter_theme: The close of the plea to the Lord. The பாரேனோ run finishes the description of Siva's form from the throat upward (the blue throat, the moon face, the lips and smile, the ears and crown, Ganga and the moon, the snake, konrai, erukku and datura, the heron feather, the fire, the raised foot on Muyalagan, the hands, the Goddess as half his body, the ash and the crescent), and then turns into a run of கிட்டாதோ (shall I not gain): the day of ripening, the silence beyond speech, the self-purity beyond assault, the open space that ends burning sorrow, servitude to the devotees, and the place where inquiry, worldly care, comparison and attachment have ceased. The last verse names the Lord as the guru of grace who strikes the poet into the state beyond word and mind, and ends in praise of his feet.
structure_note: The பாரேனோ run (484 to 495) ascends the Lord's form from throat to crown and then names the feet, hands and dance; the கிட்டாதோ run (496 to 504) lists the states the poet asks for; 501 and 505 break both runs to address the Lord as குரு. The refrain stands as a separate line in 486, 490, 494, 498 and 502.

484.reading: Shall I not see the cause of the throat that stood darkened? Shall I not see the sight of him standing in the devotees' company?
484.nuance: கண்டம் கறுத்து நின்ற காரணம் is the poison swallowed at the churning of the ocean; the poet asks to see the cause, not just the throat, so the mark is read as an act of saving. The second line puts the Lord among his devotees, the place 469 asked for.

485.reading: Shall I not see the face, a great moon ripe with grace? Shall I not see the rich fullness of the holy eyes and the matted hair?
485.nuance: அருள் பழுத்த மாமதி, the great moon ripened with grace, makes the face the moon and the moon a fruit. Line 2, திருநயனச் சடையளிருஞ் செழுங்கொழுமை, is garbled; it seems to join the eyes and hair in one phrase of fullness, but the words do not parse cleanly.

486.reading: Shall I not see the beauty growing in the red hollow's piece? Shall I not see the lip that outdid the red fruit?
486.nuance: செங்குழியின் துண்டம் is unclear: the red hollow may be the mouth and its piece the tongue, or the cheek and its dimple. அங்கனி is the red fruit (the கொவ்வை) to which lips are compared in love poetry; the Lord's form is praised in the idiom used for a beloved.

487.reading: Shall I not see the light of the smile that casts jasmine moonlight? Shall I not see the beauty of the dark brows?
487.nuance: மூரல் is the gentle smile and முல்லை நிலவு its white light, jasmine and moonlight in one; அல்லார் புருவம், brows like the night, keeps the inventory in the conventions of akam poetry.

488.reading: Shall I not see the ears where the makara earrings lie shining? Shall I not see the beauty of the peaked crown and the red matted hair?
488.nuance: வள்ளை, the ear (from the creeper the ear is likened to), carries the மகரகுண்டலம்; சிகர முடி, the crown like a peak, and the செஞ்சடை complete the ascent of the form begun at the feet in 479.

489.reading: Shall I not see the sight of Ganga standing with the moon? Shall I not see the way the swelling serpent is worn in the matted hair?
489.nuance: Ganga, the crescent and the cobra are the three tenants of Siva's hair; பொங்கு அரவு, the serpent that swells, is the hood spread. The verse names the attributes as things to be seen, not as myths to be told.

490.reading: Shall I not see the forest of matted hair in which the konrai blooms? Shall I not see the solitude adorned with erukku, arugu grass and datura?
490.nuance: சடைக்காடு, the hair as a forest, lets the konrai bloom in it. எருக்கு, அறுகு and ஊமத்தை are the wild and humble plants of Siva's worship, and ஏகாந்தம் (solitude, or the solitary one) names the ascetic aspect that wears them, a word 497 will ask for as a state.

491.reading: Shall I not see the festivity in which the heron feather is joined? Shall I not see the bliss of standing with fire held in the hand?
491.nuance: கொக்கிறகு, the heron's feather, is a less common ornament of Siva's hair, remembered in the Tevaram; the fire in the hand is the dancer's. கொண்டாட்டம் and ஆனந்தம், festivity and bliss, make the form a celebration, preparing the dance of 492.

492.reading: Shall I not see the lifted foot and the drum-slim waist? Shall I not see the dance upon the struck-down Muyalagan?
492.nuance: தூக்கிய கால், the raised foot, is the Nataraja's left foot, which the devotee seeks as refuge; முயலகன் is the dwarf under the planted foot, taken by tradition as ignorance or ego. துடியிடை, the waist slim as a துடி drum, is the love poet's word for a woman's waist applied to the dancer.

493.reading: Shall I not see the swinging hand and its opening gesture? Shall I not see the hand of refuge that grants what is desired?
493.nuance: வீசும் கரம் is the dancer's swung hand that points to the raised foot, and விகசிதம் (blossoming) may be its open gesture or the face's radiance. அபயகரம் is the hand of fearlessness; ஆசை அளிக்கும் can mean that it grants desires or that it gives love, and the second suits a hand of refuge better.

494.reading: Shall I not see the great beauty that grows in the half that is the great Mother, while Hari and Brahma praise and the gods cry 'victory, victory'?
494.nuance: பெரியம்மை பாகம், the Mother's half, is the Ardhanari form, and the beauty is said to grow (வளர்) in it. The gods' acclaim places the form at the dance; the hymn ends its inventory with the Goddess, so the form is complete only as a pair.

495.reading: Shall I not see the splendour of the fine holy ash? Shall I not see his showing of mercy as the one who wears the moon?
495.nuance: சந்திரசேகரன், the moon-crested, is given as the form in which the Lord shows தயவு, mercy, as the Puranic story of his sheltering the waning moon has it. The ash that 467 begged for is now seen on the Lord himself, closing the பாரேனோ run.

496.reading: Though the ruined days are ruined, look now with pity; though the days of suffering were suffered, will the feet not come to me?
496.nuance: The verse answers the போதாதோ litany: whatever the past has been, கிருபை is asked for now (இனி). பதம் may be the feet or the state; the கிட்டாதோ run that follows takes it as state and lists what the state contains.

497.reading: Will the day that brings me to ripeness not come to me? Will the solitude that has whirled through every season not come to me?
497.nuance: நற்பருவம், the good season, is the ripeness of the soul for grace, in Siddhanta the moment when the impurity's hold matures and falls. எப்பருவமும் சுழன்ற ஏகாந்தம் is unclear: the solitude that has passed through every season, or the solitude in which all seasons turn; either way ஏகாந்தம், the Lord's aspect in 490, is now the state asked for.

498.reading: Will the silence that stands beyond speech not come to me? Will the self-purity that stands beyond assault not come to me?
498.nuance: வாக்கிறந்து நின்ற மவுனம் places silence past speech rather than as its absence. தற்சுத்தி, purity of the self, is the complement of the malam crushed in 476; தாக்கிறந்து, beyond being struck, is answered in 505 by the guru who strikes.

499.reading: Will the open space that ends burning sorrow not come to me? Will the clarity that ends even the mind not come to me?
499.nuance: வெட்டவெளி, the bare open expanse, is the Siddhars' word for the state beyond form, the அருள்வெளி of Tirumanthiram 123. தேறல் is clarity, but also honey or liquor; on that reading the line asks for the drink that ends thought, the nectar of the yogic texts. Both readings stand.

500.reading: Will being taken as a slave by the devotees who have become not come to me? Will being made to realise, without defect, not come to me?
500.nuance: ஆன அடியார், the devotees who have become (the Lord, or complete), are the ஓங்கு பரத்துள் ஒளித்த அடியார் of 470; the poet still asks only to be their slave. உணர்த்துவித்தல், being caused to realise, is the Siddhanta term for the Lord's making the soul know.

501.reading: What shall I say? My guru, hear me: after this I have nothing else at all but you.
501.nuance: The Lord addressed as the shrine's master is named குரு here and at 505, so the one who gives the states listed is the teacher. நீ அல்லாமல் பிறிதிலை, nothing but you, is the lament's confession of sole refuge, in the plain voice the runs have been building toward.

502.reading: Will the place where that inquiry dries up not come to me? Will the place where the inquiry one speaks is lost not come to me?
502.nuance: விசாரம் is both worry and inquiry (vichara); அன்ன விசாரம், that inquiry, may refer back to the questions of 501 or to the mind's worrying in general. சொன்ன விசாரம் தொலைதல், the loss of the inquiry that is spoken, reads best as the end of doctrinal questioning, which the சொல் of 498 and 504 supports.

503.reading: Will the place where worldly care has ceased not come to me? Will not being bewitched even by the lightning-women of the troop of impurity not come to me?
503.nuance: மலக்குழுவின் மின்னார், women bright as lightning who belong to the company of impurity, picks up 450 to 452: freedom from their spell is asked for as a state to be given, not a discipline to be done. வசியாமை is not being charmed, the word for a spell.

504.reading: Will the place where comparison and attachment have ceased not come to me? Will the place of clarity that is beyond telling not come to me?
504.nuance: ஒப்புவமை, comparison and likeness, ending is the end of thinking by analogy, after a whole chapter of comparisons for the Lord's form. செப்புதற்கும் எட்டாது, out of reach even of saying, closes the list of states at the edge of language.

505.reading: Guru of grace who strikes me so that I go into the state without sorrow, beyond word and mind: to your paired feet alone I offer praise.
505.nuance: வாக்கு மனாதீத, past word and mind, is the Upanishadic formula for the Supreme. வசோகசத்து is unclear: taken as அசோக சத்து it is the sorrowless being; the text may be corrupt. தாக்கும், striking, makes the guru's grace a blow, the answer to the self-purity beyond striking in 498. The final போற்றி turns the whole lament into a hymn.

links.note: Tirumular has Muyalakan lying under the dancer whose body is space and whose hands are the eight directions; Pattinathar asks to see the dance on the struck-down Muyalagan with the lifted foot and slim waist. The cosmic and the iconic Nataraja, one dwarf under each.

The gods delighting in the konrai-haired one who shares half his body with the bright-browed lady, in Tirumular's invocation; Pattinathar's gods cry victory as the beauty grows in the great Mother's half, after the konrai in 490.

Tirumular: when the truth beyond speech is attained the five hard to curb subside and knowledge shines; Pattinathar asks for the silence beyond speech and the self-purity beyond assault as the states that would end the senses' refusal of 444.
Tirumular's Lord gave the open space of grace in great bliss, last in a list of gifts; Pattinathar's வெட்டவெளி that ends burning sorrow is the same expanse, asked for rather than received.

Tirumular asks the Lord to stand where he can be seen, since who else is kin to his servant; Pattinathar, after asking to see the form, says he has nothing but the Lord. The same claim of sole refuge, in both cases attached to seeing.

Tirumular's Lord ended word and feeling and set him in the form beyond, so that 'we passed beyond words'; Pattinathar's guru of grace strikes him into the state beyond word and mind. Both make the passage past language the Lord's act.

Tirumular's Supreme told him the one thing beyond telling and entered him; Pattinathar's Lord is named guru in the act of striking him into what is beyond word and mind. In both the guru gives what cannot be said.

source_issues: 485 line 2 திருநயனச் சடையளிருஞ் செழுங்கொழுமை does not parse and is probably corrupt.
498 line 1 வாக்கிற்து is a misprint for வாக்கிறந்து, as the parallel தாக்கிறந்து in line 2 shows.
505 line 1 வசோகசத்திற் is obscure, perhaps for அசோக சத்து.
The refrain கன்னிவனநாதா is printed as a separate line inside 486, 490, 494, 498 and 502.
